title: Witness assignment a=b=c=d=6/5 for USAMO 1978 P1
intent: Close the membership half of IsGreatest - that max_e = 16/5 is actually attained - by naming the maximising assignment with four use (6 / 5) witnesses and discharging its two defining equations with one constructor <;> norm_num.

parent.name: usa1978_p1
parent.statement: problem usa1978_p1 : IsGreatest { e : ℝ | ∃ a b c d : ℝ, IsGood a b c d e } max_e

children.name: witness a = b = c = d = 6 / 5
children.statement: the four existential variables of ∃ a b c d : ℝ, IsGood a b c d max_e (e is the set's bound variable, fixed at max_e)

applicability.goal_shape: ∃ a b c d : ℝ, IsGood a b c d max_e (reached from IsGreatest's membership conjunct via unfold + constructor + simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq])
applicability.use_when: a concrete closed-form witness is known - a maximising/minimising assignment, often with variables equal by symmetry - so use w fixes the value and leaves only the witness's defining equations, which norm_num/linarith close
applicability.avoid_when: the object's existence needs a theorem (intermediate value, fixed point, choice) rather than an explicit value, or checking that the candidate satisfies the predicate is itself substantial

claims.claim: The membership branch of usa1978_p1 closes in six lines - four use (6 / 5) and one constructor <;> norm_num - with no named lemma and no manual rewriting.

claims.claim: The authors give the informal plan as a comment citing 'solution 3 from https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/1978_USAMO_Problems/Problem_1', and the formal use (6 / 5) reproduces that solution's assignment a = b = c = d = 6/5, e = 16/5.
The witness move carries the whole 'max_e is attained' direction in 6 lines (41-46) against 21 lines (47-67) for the upper-bound direction.

consequences: Replaces ∃ x, P x by P w for the chosen witness, so a wrong value makes the goal unprovable and must be fixed first (6/5 is forced by e = 16/5 and the two equations; the four equalities rely on the solution's symmetry). The witness must satisfy every conjunct of the predicate: IsGood's two equations close together under constructor <;> norm_num, and if one were not norm_num-solvable the shared <;> would leave a goal. The witness only covers the attained half of IsGreatest; the upper-bound half is a separate argument.
